note: 18 numbered exhibits (12 plates, 6 grids) on 27 measured regions over 21 pages; 9 regions excluded (7 fragments of multi-panel plates, 2 newspaper images).
rules: Twelve plates in five families - flowchart-or-schematic 5 (Figs. 1, 2, 3, 5, 8), line 2 (Figs. 4, 12), scatter 2 (Figs. 6, 9), heatmap-or-contour 2 (Figs. 10, 11), map-or-plan-view 1 (Fig. 7) - and the six printed grids form the sixth register [geometry.family].
Caption side follows the medium without a single exception: all 12 plates print their caption BELOW the plate and all 6 grids print theirs ABOVE [caption.position].

Every caption is one bare noun phrase in the house form 'Figure N:' or 'Table N:'; the paper never abbreviates to 'Fig.', never drops the colon and never ends a caption with a period [caption.numbering] [caption.sentences].

No caption states a unit, a condition or a conclusion, and none is written in the active or passive voice; one caption, Table 2, names a variable (VI) [caption.units] [caption.conditions] [caption.concludes] [caption.voice] [caption.variables].

Five of the eight numbered pointers name the WRONG exhibit - 'Figure 4' for Fig. 5, 'Figure 5' for Fig. 6, 'Figure 7' for Fig. 9, 'Figure 8' for Fig. 10 and 'Table 3' for Table 4 - and only Figure 4, Table 1 and Table 2 are cited by their own number [mention.style] [mention.first_page].

Seven exhibits are pointed at only by a deictic phrase with no number at all - 'the figure below' (Fig. 1), 'The diagram below' (Fig. 3), 'as below' (Table 3), 'shown below' (Table 5), 'the table below' (Table 6), 'graphs below' (Fig. 12) and 'this point on the GE matrix' (Fig. 11) - so a reader who trusts the numbering is misled and a reader who trusts the pointing is never told the number [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.lead_sentence].

Three exhibits are never named in prose at all - the paper-structure diagram (Fig. 2), the world map (Fig. 7) and the ESE hexagon (Fig. 8) - and all three are artwork whose caption carries the whole message [mention.count].

Grids are horizontal-rule tables and nothing else: booktabs rules, no verticals, no boxing, no zebra striping, full text width, portrait [table.rule_style] [table.zebra] [table.width] [table.orientation].

Table furniture appears once each rather than habitually - one diagonal header (Table 2, VI over Em), one merged stub column (Table 3, four merged dimension cells), one grid continued across a page break (Table 2) - and no grid puts a unit in its header [table.diagonal_header] [table.merged_cells] [table.continued] [table.units_in_header].
Grid size tracks the datum, not the page: the measured grids run 3 to 12 rows by 2 to 7 columns, and the two biggest are the two whose print runs past their measured band [table.rows] [table.cols].

Four pointers arrive a page before the exhibit: '(Figure 7)' for Fig. 9, '(Table 2)' for Table 2, 'shown below' for Table 5 and 'this point on the GE matrix' for Fig. 11 all sit on the page before [mention.lead_pages].

No plate is drawn in three dimensions and none carries a colour bar, yet one scatter plots its points as pseudo-3-D spheres on a flat plane, so the depth cue is decoration [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar] [geometry.printed_numbers].
